chunks: From him, from Muḥammad ibn al-Ḥusayn, from ʿAmmār ibn al-Mubārak, from Muḥammad ibn ʿUdhāfir, from Isḥāq ibn ʿAmmār, who said:

I said to Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: I rise when dawn has already come, and I have not performed Ṣalāt al-Layl. He said: Perform Ṣalāt al-Layl, and perform the witr, and perform the two rakʿahs of dawn.

So these two reports were transmitted as a concession regarding the permissibility of delaying Ṣalāt al-Ghadāt from the beginning of its time, because that is permissible in cases of excuses, as we have mentioned before; and among the excuses is making up Ṣalāt al-Layl. However, what we mentioned earlier is more excellent, and that which also indicates this concession is:

key_terms.أَوْتِرْ: perform the witr prayer, the closing unit of the night prayer
key_terms.الْأَعْذَارِ: excuses that justify departure from the preferred timing
key_terms.الْفَجْرُ: dawn, the start of the morning prayer time
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيِ الْفَجْرِ: the two rakʿahs associated with dawn before the obligatory morning prayer
key_terms.رُخْصَةً: a legal concession granted in circumstances of excuse
key_terms.صَلَاةَ اللَّيْلِ: the night prayer performed in the late night hours
key_terms.قَضَاءُ: making up an act of worship after its usual time

ai.seo_question: Can Ṣalāt al-Ghadāt be delayed in order to make up Ṣalāt al-Layl after dawn?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of one who wakes after the break of dawn without having performed Ṣalāt al-Layl. Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام permits him to perform the night prayer, the witr, and then the two rakʿahs of dawn, and the compiler explains this as a rukhsah allowing delay of the morning prayer from its earliest time due to an excuse.
